MIGRATION 0064 (apps/api/migrations/0064_account_deletion.sql, 0063 was still highest). Deviations / pg-mem fallbacks: (1) Views use CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW instead of DROP VIEW IF EXISTS + CREATE VIEW, because pg-mem has no DROP VIEW and cannot replace an existing view; first apply works in pg-mem with no test-side stripping, so repo tests of later features can apply 0001..0064 verbatim. migration0064.test.ts reapplies the file with the view statements skipped and asserts the CREATE OR REPLACE text. Recorded as a note in design.md DDL notes. (2) The id::text LIKE 'deadc0de-%' CHECK IS accepted and enforced by pg-mem (valid and invalid rows tested), so NO fallback was taken and nothing needs moving to ensureTombstone. (3) pg-mem does NOT backfill a NOT NULL DEFAULT column onto rows that existed before the ALTER (they read back NULL); Postgres does. So 'existing rows default to active' is asserted from the DDL text; defaults of newly inserted rows are asserted by query. Do not write later tests that depend on a pre-existing pg-mem row getting deletion_state='active' (apply migrations first, then insert). pg-mem accepted all 64 migrations with the gin-index and AT TIME ZONE stripping used by migration0063.test.ts (the helper is copied into migration0064.test.ts: buildPgMemDatabase + applyMigration).
